internal_discovery.plain_explanation:
Every occurrence is nominal (form N) and instantiates one of five lexeme-types of the doubled root, all reducing to the same charge-relation.

(1) rabb + suffix/idafa (the mass, ~971). The residue surfaces in all its facets. OWNERSHIP/MASTERY over a person: Joseph's house-master "innahu rabbi ahsana mathwaya" (12:23), the king as a servant's rabb "yasqi rabbahu khamran" / "udhkurni inda rabbik" / "irji ila rabbik" (12:41,42,50). SUSTENANCE/PROVISION: the tree yields "bi-idhni rabbiha" (14:25); "ta'adhdhana rabbukum la-in shakartum la-azidannakum" (14:7); the rabb who "yabsutu l-rizqa" (17:30). GOVERNANCE/DIRECTION: "wa-awha rabbuka ila l-nahl" — directing even the bee (16:68); "qada rabbuka alla ta'budu illa iyyah" (17:23); "amru rabbik" as executive command (11:101; 16:33). REARING TO COMPLETION: "yajtabika rabbuka wa-yu'allimuka ... wa-yutimmu ni'matahu alayk" (12:6). The same word names FALSE/CANDIDATE masters when a creature is wrongly treated as the governing charge-holder: "hadha rabbi" of star and sun (6:76-78).

(2) arbab (plural, 4x): the identical relation predicated of illegitimate multiple masters — "alla yattakhidha ba'duna ba'dan arbaban min duni llah" (3:64), angels/prophets as arbab (3:80), rabbis and monks taken as arbab (9:31), "a-arbabun mutafarriqun khayrun am Allahu l-wahid" (12:39). Subtracting plural morphology and the polemical context leaves "masters holding authoritative charge."

(3) rabbaniyy (nisba, 3x): "kunu rabbaniyyina bima kuntum tu'allimuna l-kitab" (3:79); "al-rabbaniyyuna wal-ahbar" charged with guarding/judging by God's book (5:44), and rebuked for failing to restrain wrongdoing (5:63). The -iyy nisba orients the charge-relation two ways at once, both internal to rbb: persons belonging-under/devoted-to the Rabb, and persons who themselves exercise a rearing/teaching charge over others (paired with teaching and guarding scripture).

(4) ribbiyyun (nisba, 1x): "qatala ma'ahu ribbiyyuna kathir" (3:146) — devoted companies fighting alongside a prophet; a nisba to the same base, "those belonging to the Rabb / under the master's cause."

(5) rabaib (1x): "wa-rabaibukumu llati fi hujurikum" (4:23) — step-daughters explicitly glossed by the text as those "in your care/laps." This is the passive pole of the very same relation: the female reared and held in a guardian's custodial charge. It is the decisive internal witness that the root's "rear/sustain" facet is not imported but attested, and that the abstract center genuinely fuses governance with rearing.

Across all five, subtract morphology, construction, participants and context and the same non-empty invariant remains: X stands in a proprietary-sustaining-governing charge over Y (or, passively, Y is held/reared under X).
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM: rabb is the intensive/agentive fa'l noun ("the one characterized by the rbb-charge"); arbab is its broken plural (multiplicity of holders); rabbaniyy/ribbiyy are nisba adjectives ("belonging to / oriented by the charge-relation"); rabiba/rabaib is a fa'ila form with passive orientation ("the one reared/held"). Subtracting agent-vs-patient diathesis, singular/plural, and nisba leaves the bare relation. CONSTRUCTION: idafa (rabbu l-'alamin, rabbuka, rabbaha) supplies only the OBJECT of the charge (whose/of-what); prepositional frames add directional vectors that are NOT the residue — bi-rabbihim = belief IN the charge-holder (14:18), ila rabbihim = return TO him (11:23), 'ala rabbihim yatawakkalun = reliance UPON him (16:42), 'inda rabbik = position BEFORE him (11:83). Strip these and the noun still denotes only "the one holding charge." PARTICIPANTS: God (overwhelmingly), human masters (Joseph's master, the king), false lords (celestial bodies, arbab), devout teachers (rabbaniyyun), fighting bands (ribbiyyun), and the reared step-daughter (rabaib). Identity is contextual, not part of the residue. CONTEXT: creation, provision, judgment, supplication (rabbana), oath (fa-wa-rabbik 15:92), law (4:23), narrative (Joseph, Abraham). All strippable. Invariant after subtraction: custodial-sustaining mastership.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: rabaib at 4:23:20:2 ("wa-rabaibukumu llati fi hujurikum"). It is hardest because its referent is the OBJECT of the charge (a step-daughter), not the charge-HOLDER (master/lord) that every other occurrence names; on a naive gloss "rbb = lord" it looks contradicted (a step-daughter is not a lord). It reconciles cleanly by FORM-layer subtraction: rabiba is a fa'ila form with passive orientation, the correlative pole of the same rbb relation — "the one reared and held in custodial charge." The residue "custodial-rearing charge" is fully present; only the diathesis (agent vs patient of the relation) flips, which is morphology, not a root contradiction. The verse's own gloss "fi hujurikum" ("in your care") makes the charge-relation surface-explicit. Far from breaking the unity, this occurrence supplies the internal bridge proving the "rear/sustain" facet of the abstract center.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The strongest alternative is a single narrower core: either (a) pure OWNERSHIP/DOMINION (malik/mulk-like possession) or (b) pure AUTHORITY / OBEYED-CHIEF (sayyid to be obeyed). Each covers a large slice: (a) fits the possessive human-master cases and arbab; (b) fits "fa-l-ya'budu rabba hadha l-bayt" (106:3), "qada rabbuka" (17:23), and arbab. But internal evidence arbitrates against either alone and for the union: pure ownership cannot absorb the active provisioning/rearing/perfecting data (14:7 "if you thank I will increase you"; 16:68 inspiring the bee; 12:6 choosing, teaching and completing; rabaib being reared). Pure authority/command cannot absorb the sustenance data (rizq bestowed; the tree fed "bi-idhni rabbiha") nor the passive reared pole (rabaib). Because both poles are co-attested within the same lexeme set, the data forces the fused center "custodial mastership = own + sustain + govern + rear," which dominates either isolated sub-sense.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest neighbors and the line against each: (1) m-l-k (malik/mulk) = sovereign possession/dominion — a malik may own and rule by title/power without any sustaining or rearing; rbb foregrounds the custodial provision-and-cultivation of what is held (the rabb feeds, guides and brings to completion). (2) s-w-d (sayyid) = chief/master-to-be-obeyed, i.e. social precedence and obedience — overlaps at "obeyed master" but lacks the proprietary + provisioning + rearing core. (3) '-l-h (ilah) = deity as object of worship — the Qur'an keeps these distinct: 9:31 rebukes taking scholars as arbab "though commanded to worship one ilah," and rbb applies to non-worshipped human masters (Joseph's master); rbb is the sustaining-charge argued to GROUND worship, not worship-worthiness itself. (4) w-l-y (waliyy) = guardian/ally/protector through nearness — protective alliance, not commanding-owning-rearing charge. (5) kh-l-q / r-z-q = create / provide are ACTS a rabb performs, not the standing relation. Falsifiability: the residue is refuted if any occurrence denotes rbb where the referent stands in NO custodial/charge relation to another entity (rabb of a mere equal, an unrelated stranger, a bare sovereign title stripped of any sustaining/directing dimension, or an abstract quality with no held object). No such occurrence exists across the 980; every one supplies, by idafa or context, an entity held in charge — or, in rabaib, an entity held.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty contribution — custodial mastership (owner–sustainer–governor–rearer of a held entity, with a passive reared pole) — is recoverable in every one of the 980 occurrences after clean layer-subtraction, and it is surface-transparent in the overwhelming mass, which are rabb/arbab literally denoting master/lord. Direction is determinate: the noun names the party in whose charge another stands (or, in rabaib, the party held), never a directionless quality. The apparent two-headedness (govern vs rear) is not an external abstraction but is internally co-attested: human ownership (Joseph's master, the king), active provision (the fed tree 14:25; increase for gratitude 14:7), executive direction (the bee 16:68; qada rabbuka 17:23), rearing to completion (12:6), and the explicitly custodial reared step-daughters "fi hujurikum" (4:23) together force a fused center rather than any isolated sub-sense — so the competing narrow hypotheses (pure ownership; pure obeyed-authority) are arbitrated out by the data itself. The only occurrences needing more than surface reading are the passive pole rabaib (diathesis flip, a form-layer feature) and the nisba forms rabbaniyy/ribbiyy (light "belonging-to / exercising charge" inference); both reconcile by morphology without forcing, leaving no residue-absent case. The contribution is sharply distinct from its neighbors m-l-k, s-w-d, '-l-h, w-l-y with a stated falsifiability condition that no occurrence meets. Because presence is genuine and largely surface-recoverable, the direction determinate, and the distinction sharp, the disposition is PREFERRED at STRONG strength; the sole reservation short of trivial is that the unifying center is a fusion of governance and cultivation rather than one atomic gloss, but that fusion is itself evidenced within the data, so no anomaly is hidden and inconsistent_refs is empty.

adversarial_verification.notes:
REFUTATION SWEEP. Coverage: form is uniformly N across all 980; the semantic space collapses to the five lexeme-types named. I inspected verbatim every non-rabb form (arbab 3:64:22:1, 3:80:7:1, 9:31:4:1, 12:39:3:2; rabbaniyy 3:79:21:1, 5:44:14:3, 5:63:3:2; ribbiyyun 3:146:6:1; rabaib 4:23:20:2), the false-master cluster (6:76-78 hadha rabbi), the human-master cluster (12:23/41/42/50), and sampled the divine-rabb mass at the head and middle. 

WHERE THE CANDIDATE HOLDS. The ~971 rabb+idafa/suffix occurrences robustly instantiate the fused charge-relation: Allah as creator-owner (10:3), provider (14:7, 17:30), executive governor (11:101 amr rabbik; 17:23 qada rabbuk; 16:68 awha rabbuka ila l-nahl), and rearer-to-completion (12:6 yutimmu ni'matah). Supplication vocatives (rabbi/rabbana) and "ajruhum inda rabbihim" address exactly the sustaining/governing charge-holder. Human masters (Joseph's aziz 12:23; the king 12:41/42/50) supply the pure ownership/authority pole; false candidates (star/sun/moon 6:76-78; arbab ×4) are the SAME relation wrongly predicated. rabaib (4:23) is textually glossed "fi hujurikum/care" and matches the pre-declared passive reared pole — it SUPPORTS, not refutes, the rear/sustain facet. No homonymy: all forms plausibly descend from the one doubled root and share the lord/master/rear thread, so REFUTED is not warranted.

WHY NOT SUPPORTED (real problems). (1) The nisba forms occupy the AFFILIATE/devotee role — persons DEFINED BY belonging/devotion to the Rabb — which is the inverse of the frozen invariant's "party who HOLDS proprietary-sustaining-governing charge over another." The discovery concedes this by adding an ad-hoc "belonging-under/devoted-to" pole distinct from the passive-reared (rabiba) pole it originally defined, and by having rabbaniyy "orient two ways at once." That two-directional, tri-positional elasticity (master / reared-subject / devotee-affiliate) is over-breadth: the four-facet fusion is applied DISJUNCTIVELY, so almost any occurrence can be absorbed. (2) ribbiyyun (3:146:6:1) is the single clearest failure: the referents neither hold nor are reared-under any charge — they merely fight alongside a prophet; they are saved only by the affiliate re-label, AND a well-attested competing derivation reads ribbiyyun as "large multitudes/companies" (from ribbah), a numeric/collective sense the custodial-mastership gloss cannot bridge. I list it. (3) The rabbaniyy trio (3:79/5:44/5:63) is milder and partly rescuable via an ACTIVE charge textually present (teaching the Book 3:79; entrusted-to-guard istuhfizu 5:44; failing to restrain sin 5:63), but their primary lexical sense is "godly/devoted-to-the-Lord" (affiliate direction), so they still stress the master-holder wording; I list them with that caveat. (4) The "single FUSED relation" claim overstates: no occurrence requires all four facets simultaneously — rabaib carries only rearing, the nisbas only affiliation/derived-charge — so the "fusion" is an analyst's union, textured only in the divine core.

NEIGHBOR-ROOT CONTRAST (distinctiveness holds overall). rbb is discriminable from m-l-k (bare ownership/kingship, no rearing/sustaining nuance), '-m-r (bare command), '-l-h (worship-worthiness — the candidate rightly excludes this; worship in 106:3 etc. FOLLOWS from the charge, is not its content), w-l-y (patronage/guardianship without the ownership+rearing fusion), and pure nurture roots (n-sh-'/gh-dh-w). The negative clauses give it teeth, so distinctiveness_ok=true and falsifiable=true (a bare-title/bare-command/unrelated-sense occurrence would falsify it; I tested this against ribbiyyun). But the fraying at the nisbas is why the overall verdict is PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED rather than SUPPORTED.

لِمَنْ خَشِىَ رَبَّهُۥ 'for whoever feared his Lord' — the master held in awe by the one under charge; charge-relation present.
جَزَآؤُهُمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ 'their reward with their Lord' — the master granting recompense; ownership/sustainer facet present.
بِأَنَّ رَبَّكَ أَوْحَىٰ لَهَا 'that your Lord inspired it (the earth)' — directing even the earth; governance-direction facet present.
رَبُّ ٱلْعَرْشِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ 'Lord of the mighty throne' — idafa of ownership/mastery over the throne; ownership facet present.
يُبَشِّرُهُمْ رَبُّهُم 'their Lord gives them glad tidings' of mercy and gardens — the sustaining master bestowing bounty; sustenance facet present.

أَرْبَابًا 'they took their rabbis and monks as lords beside God' — plural of the identical relation predicated of illegitimate masters; subtract plural morphology and polemic, residue 'masters holding authoritative charge' remains.
